tagline: Route 28N to North Creek, on Roosevelt's overnight ride of 1901.
intro: From the hamlet of Long Lake, Route 28N heads east through the middle of the park, south of Rich Lake and into Newcomb, then bends south past Vanderwhacker Mountain, through Aiden Lair and Minerva, and crosses the Hudson into North Creek. Much of it began as the old highway from Warren County to Long Lake, along which Newcomb's first settlers built, and the state took it on as early as 1909.

On September 10, 1901, Vice President Theodore Roosevelt came this way by wagon, overnight, after word reached him that McKinley, shot four days earlier in Buffalo, was near death. At the North Creek station he learned he was to be president.

moments.title: Goodnow Mountain
moments.text: A 60-foot steel fire tower went up on the 2,664-foot summit in 1922, stopped watching for fires after 1979, and has since been restored and opened to the public.

moments.title: Santanoni Preserve
moments.text: At the edge of Newcomb a stone gateway arch leads into Camp Santanoni, once reckoned the grandest of the Adirondack great camps and now a National Historic Landmark.

moments.title: North Creek
moments.text: The road ends at the old northern terminus of the Adirondack Railway, the first railroad into the mountains, whose station complex is on the National Register.
